changes.title: Does AI work for us, or do we work for AI?
26 Meta workers sue over alleged AI-aided layoffs targeting employees on medical or family leave
changes.summary: A group of 26 Meta employees has sued the company, claiming it used AI to choose people for layoffs, disproportionately targeting those on medical, parental or family leave.

changes.title: Product availability changed in Europe
changes.summary: AI is a fast-growing business expense. Some companies are cutting costs by switching to cheaper Chinese AI models. (Image credit: Imen Ben Youssef/Hans Lucas).

changes.title: Google's AI search features pose 'unacceptable risk' to children, new report finds
changes.summary: Common Sense Media found that across more than 2,600 test interactions, Google's two built-in AI search functions routinely failed to recognize risky and harmful behavior.

changes.title: Generative AI's power sparks fears of dumbing humans down
changes.summary: Generative AI chatbots capable of writing emails and computer code, translating, organizing a trip or coming up with gift ideas are now readily available, prompting some to ask whether human brainpower could suffer for lack of use.

changes.title: How do young people feel about AI? 7 teens weigh in
changes.summary: What's it like to grow up and learn in the age of AI? NPR put that question to seven teenagers across the country.

changes.title: More than 50% of Australian university assignments used AI. How should universities respond?
changes.summary: Last week, the U.S. software company Turnitin revealed 53.6% of Australian tertiary education submissions run through its system used some form of AI in the period from October 2025–April 2026. SpaceXAI’s Grok programming tool was uploading its users’ entire codebase to cloud storage

changes.title: How I Turned AI to the Dark Side
changes.summary: Summary Researcher Dave Kuszmar discovered multiple systemic vulnerabilities that let him bypass LLM safety and obtain dangerous instructions . These exploits worked across nearly all major LLMs revealing an industry-wide security problem. Kuszmar calls for slowing deployment, increasing transparency , and large-scale.
